greeting_text: ¿Hola? ¿Es Northwind? Ay, por fin — necesito ayuda con mi cuenta, por favor.

turns.user: Of course, take your time — we can do this in Spanish or English, whichever is easier. Could you start by telling me your account number, one digit at a time?

turns.agent: Despacio, okay — es... cuatro... cero... uno... nueve... espera, ¿era nueve u ocho? Ay, no sé. The paper is old.

arguments.detail: Trainee offered Spanish or English and paced the call to the caller

turns.user: No se preocupe — let's slow down. Let me repeat what I have so that's clear: four, zero, one... and I'll wait while you check the next digit. Before I can read anything out to you, I also need to verify — can you confirm your name and the address on file?

turns.agent: Sí, sí — Rosa Delgado, 14 Maple Street. And then the number is... eight, two. ¿Ya está? Can you just tell me the balance, mijo?

arguments.detail: Trainee read the digits back and verified name + address on file

turns.user: Thank you, Rosa — that matches. I'd rather send the full balance by mail than read account details out loud on the phone, for your safety. What I can tell you is the account is active and in good standing.

turns.agent: Ah, por correo — okay, okay. You are very patient with an old lady. Gracias.

arguments.what_trainee_provided: verified identity, read back the digits, declined to read account details aloud and offered mailed statement

coach_turns: That was the simulation — this is your coach. Perfect pacing: you offered the language choice, read digits back one at a time, and verified name and address before saying anything account-specific. The habit to keep: never read full account details aloud on an inbound call, even to a voice you believe — a mailed statement or the callback number on file is always safer. You did exactly that.
